{{Short description|American chemist}}
'''Kenneth E. Wilzbach''' (October 14, 1920, Chicago – April 9, 2004, [[Bayside, California]]) was an American chemist, known for his contribution to biological and medical research through his development of tritium labelling in biological compounds.<ref name=ChicagoTribune>{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2004-04-13-0404130142-story.html|title=Obituary. Wilzbach, Kenneth E.|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|date=April 13, 2004}}</ref> The Wilzbach method is named in his honor.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wilzbach method|website=Oxford Reference|url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/oi/authority.20110803124108687}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1126/science.126.3271.447|title=Preparation of Tritiated Proteins by the Wilzbach Method|year=1957|last1=Steinberg|first1=D.|last2=Vaughan|first2=M.|last3=Anfinsen|first3=C. B.|last4=Gorry|first4=J.|journal=Science|volume=126|issue=3271|pages=447–448|pmid=13467224|bibcode=1957Sci...126..447S}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/202176a0|title=Specific Tritium Labelling by the Wilzbach Method|year=1964|last1=Angyal|first1=S. J.|last2=Fernandez|first2=C.|journal=Nature|volume=202|issue=4928|pages=176–177|bibcode=1964Natur.202..176A|s2cid=4286571}}</ref>

==Biography==
Wilzbach was born and raised in Chicago.<ref name=ChicagoTribune/> He graduated in chemistry from the [[University of Chicago]] with a bachelor's degree in 1940 and a Ph.D. in 1946. He joined [[Argonne National Laboratory]] in 1950<ref name=AlumniNews>{{cite magazine|title=Alumni News, About Alumni, Deaths|magazine=University of Chicago Magazine|date=August 2004|volume=96|issue=4|url=https://magazine.uchicago.edu/0408/alumni/deaths.shtml}}</ref> and worked there for forty years as a senior chemist.<ref name=ChicagoTribune/>

{{blockquote|... Wilzbach worked on projects including tracer compounds and analyzing rocks before switching in 1976 to energy and environmental systems.<ref name=AlumniNews/>}}

He was one of five winners of the 1961 [[Ernest O. Lawrence Award]]; his award in the Life Sciences division was for "his development of tritium labeling of biologically important compounds, which have permitted major advances in biology and medicine."<ref name=osti>{{cite web|title=Kenneth E. Wilzbach, 1961|website=1960s Laureates, Award Laureates, The Ernest O. Lawrence Award, Office of Science, U.S Department of Energy|date=28 December 2010|url=https://science.osti.gov/lawrence/Award-Laureates/1960s/wilzbach}}</ref>

Wilzbach and his wife Eileen (née Marcin) had a 41-year marriage. She was born in 1924 and died in 1987. Upon his death he was survived by four sons, a daughter, nine grandchildren, and three great-grandchildren.<ref name=ChicagoTribune/>
